extraction.segment_function: Introduction, intellectual context, and paper hypothesis concerning Hannah Arendt's interpretation of the natural and the artificial in The Human Condition.

claims.claim: Modernity has traditionally been presented as the age when artifacts supplant nature and destroy the originally given natural environment through a process of de-naturalization, but Hannah Arendt questioned this conviction.
claims.supporting_excerpt: Modernity, in philosophical and sociological literature, has “traditionally” been presented as the age when artifacts supplant nature and destroy the originally given natural environment. The process of modernization, from this point of view, is the process of de-naturalization . This widely shared conviction has ba - sically been questioned by Hannah Arendt.

definitions.definition: The process where artifacts supplant nature and destroy the originally given natural environment.
A process taking place during the centuries of the modern age to the detriment of the commonly created and uphold human world, enhanced by technology.

distinctions.distinction: The Arendtian critique of modernity takes a difference between the notions of Earth and world.

unresolved_context: The full implications of how Heidegger's philosophy influenced Arendt's distinction between Earth and world within the broader text.
must_not_be_lost: Arendt's view that modernity is an age of world-alienation and re-naturalization rather than simply de-naturalization.
